quest.title: Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief...
quest.description: Yuften's goods appear to have been stolen by some unknown party. They need to be recovered.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x25000, Hero's Wit x3

chapter.title: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Ah, Master of the Jinni! Y—you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: I jus—just so happen to have a t—task for you... An urgent one!

choices.text: Slow down, I'm listening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, slow down! We'll help once you tell us what's happening!

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: A shipment—a shipment—a—a shipment of goods has g—gone missing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You lost three shipment of goods!?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: N—no! Just on—one shipment.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: I contracted an outside party to sh—ship us some Anahitian Blessing, b—but a l—long time has p—passed and it's s—still not here...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: It might be the d—doing of those nor—northerners... Might be retaliation because Babel is always s—searching them for t—traitors...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: E-ever since Aderfi and Azariq left... The northerners h—have been much more a—active.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: A—alright. I am d—done with dallying. The caravan delivering the Anahitian Blessing's last known location i—is in this region, according to our scouts.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: I hope you can help me f—find the goods. Or a—at—at least find any clues as to what happened to the caravan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure. I'll give you a hand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A caravan can't just disappear on its own, right? Sounds like they got robbed by some bandits...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Th—thank you. A tho—thousand thanks! Please, accept this meat as gra—gratitude for your service.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Thanks! You're too kind!

choices.text: What do you need my help with?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Take it slowly now! You don't need to hurry!

talks.objective: Head to the last known location of the merchant caravan

dialogues.speaker: Damaged Jar
dialogues.text: (A cracked, empty jar lay there, not yet swallowed by the sands. Looks like it was thrown aside not long ago.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! That jar's still poking out from the sand!

choices.text: The goods lay scattered along the trail...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, this doesn't look good... Paimon thinks that they might have dropped some other goods along the way? Maybe we should keep searching ahead.

choices.text: Let's see what we can find along this trail.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... They might have left some other stuff behind them. Let's keep going!

dialogues.speaker: Empty Broken Box
dialogues.text: (An empty, broken box lay abandoned, toppled over by the roadside.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. This box must be from the caravan. Look! It even has the tribe's symbol on it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Won't be hard to ambush someone here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... This place looks dangerous!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It looks like they stole even the largest of the goods...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They moved all the valuables, but left the containers. Huh. Paimon guesses they might have a lot of people, but don't seem to have the tools to move the crates.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Or, perhaps, this is a trap...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A... trap?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you mean they left these empty boxes on purpose? To... lure people to them?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: To lure us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Paimon's getting goosebumps! Then... do we really need to keep going...

choices.text: If you're scared, you can always turn and head back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Pfft. Paimon's not scared. Hmph. Besides, you can't just leave Paimon!

choices.text: The bandits might still be nearby.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, the way you say that isn't making Paimon feel good at all... But since you're not scared, maybe we should keep going...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: This matter is e—extremely urgent! P—please go inform the Matriarch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph... They left absolutely nothing intact. Oh, Paimon's getting mad! These hilichurls really know how to break stuff!

choices.text: Wait, it doesn't look like it was destroyed by hilichurls...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But... the hilichurls have their camp here, don't they?

choices.text: I don't see any carts around us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... You're right! There aren't any carts or even wrecks here... The shack left behind by the hilichurls also doesn't seem to have any cart parts... How strange.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's follow the road a while longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. But if it wasn't the hilichurls, then who?

choices.text: Look. No cart in the camp either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! If the hilichurls raided the caravan, they would've taken the carts apart on the spot. But we're not seeing any carts, or any parts... Paimon thinks that's kind of weird!

choices.text: Wait, the raid might not have happened here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the hilichurls placed their camp right in the middle of the road... Look there. If they block that spot off, won't it be easy to rob someone?

choices.text: I don't see any carts around us...
Look. No cart in the camp either.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Ruined Rug
dialogues.text: (A rolled carpet that's still in good condition. The symbol of the Tanit tribe is stitched into it, while ominous blotches dot its surface...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The rug... how strange...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Wow, that rug looks expensive. But why did it just get left here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe there was a struggle or fight over it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm... Yeah... Paimon thinks she can see that happening.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The caravan and the robbers had a fight here. Some goods got damaged during the battle, while other perfectly fine ones were left aside in the ensuing chaos...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very astute, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. Paimon's the best!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then, the caravan and the robbers fought while running all along the way... fighting and running and fighting... That's why all these boxes and jars are scattered everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm. Paimon thinks that's a good deduction!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't make any sense!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph!

choices.text: The trashed goods should have been discarded after the bandits got to them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Because we didn't see any signs of a struggle along the way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, that's how it was... Still, Paimon's theory was close... Like ninety-percent accurate close!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Paimon can't help feeling something's wrong...

choices.text: About what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't you... think these clues are too neatly laid out? It's like they were placed in a line to lead us over somewhere...

choices.text: You... might be a bit too suspicious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Look, the cart's right there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can barely recognize it... Though the Tanit marking's there, it looks a bit... blurry...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. We can close this case now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's elementary: What happened was that the caravan was ambushed and the goods were all stolen. Let's go back to Yuften and tell him what happened!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Right, let's head back.
Pardon me, but I beg you both to still your stride.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Who are you?
We are friends. Of Jeht's. You have been working hard.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, well, Jeht's friends are our friends! We were just finishing up! Let's head back together!
Haha, no need to be so hasty. And guests shouldn't be so harried to depart.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, wait... There's something not right with them.
Jeht requested that you stay in the desert for a time... She commissioned us to come here and give you the "hospitality" you deserve.
It would be cruel of you to disappoint her kindness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh... {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon. Hide.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Alright!

choices.text: Possibly, but we don't have enough evidence for that.
Time for Paimon to use her intuition!
The things they left behind were to ensure they moved fast and light.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... that was close. Luckily, we're good at fighting. Took them down in no time flat!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for your "hospitality."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is it that every bad guy wants to mess with us? Is it because we look soft?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They claimed to be sent by Jeht...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you believe them?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think Jeht has a reason to do this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But she might be wrapped up in something big...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Paimon doesn't think Jeht would do this either... But, what should we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The people who just ambushed us knew Jeht, which means that they must know people amongst the Tanit as well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean that if we return to the tribe, we'll catch their attention? Paimon doesn't think they'll just let this go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Jeht... Paimon's not suspecting her, but the people who tried to kill us might be hiding within the tribe. Maybe we should leave for a while...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If we leave, Jeht might be in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... We can't just leave her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go back first. But don't mention Jeht.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Paimon's not scared! If you've decided, then that's how we'll do it!

talks.objective: Report your findings back to Yuften

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Y—y—you're back?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Something strange about us coming back?

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: N—N—No. I'm v—very pleased th—that you h—have returned, e—esteemed Master of the Jinni.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: R—right. Ab—abo—about the c—caravan. How did y—your investigation... go?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The caravan got ambushed. The goods have been taken.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Cu—curses! It's those traitors again! I—I—I just kn—know it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traitors...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Th—Th—Those traitors! Those northerner colluding dogs!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: A—aside from this, wh—what else ha—have you uncovered?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We were ambushed by the Eremites.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Just as we finished investigating what happened to the caravan, the Eremites showed up to ambush us! They also said...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They also said that they knew us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right... That too!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: I—if—if that's the c—case... Th—then they might be onto you as well.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: H—Here is your pa—payment. P—Please go see Matriarch B—Babel about th—this matter as s—soon as possible!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Right.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Fa—farewell, esteemed Master of the Jinni.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Greetings, esteemed Master of the Jinni. Is there something you need?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yuften's caravan got raided by some of your traitors.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Truly... Well, it's not unexpected. The northerners from the snowlands have long tried to push into our lands. The treacherous amongst our number fell prey to their words and turned against us.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: These traitors have been causing havoc for quite some time. Sporadic but persistent raids and robberies have been happening since a few months ago...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Oh... Apologies, I didn't mean to interrupt. Please continue.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The traitors have also taken an interest in us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Just as we finished investigating the caravan, thugs from the Eremites ambushed us.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Is that the case... How vile.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: It appears that... with Aderfi and Azariq both gone, these wild dogs see this as high time to bare their teeth.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: How about this? Please wait here and rest. I will handle all matters regarding your safety.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Jeht is still outside fulfilling her duties to the tribe. I will have her work alongside you to get to the bottom of this matter.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And before that, I will do my utmost to find the assassins who sought you dead... I ask for only patience in return.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Oh, one more thing! The bad guys that jumped us seemed to know us! They might be from the tribe!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: It's not impossible... But it matters little. With your privileges as esteemed guests, you will be protected... So long as you stay here, no one can hurt you.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: If anyone of the Tanit seeks to trouble you, whoever they are, they will face judgment at my hands, under my authority as Matriarch.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Please, rest. I will pursue the matter of the traitors to the fullest of my ability.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Additionally, I will keep watch for Jeht on your behalf. I will notify you the moment she returns.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Thanks a lot, Matriarch Babel.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: The courtesy is unneeded.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: H—h—how's your search going?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're still looking for the caravan.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Pl—p—please find them. I beg you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! How have you been!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Thanks for adventuring with me. I... about my parents... Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no need.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah. If Babel didn't have me doing commissions for other assignments, I would be exploring the desert right alongside you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I still know plenty of cool places! When I find the time, I'll show them to you!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It's just... now's not the time. The cursed traitors are colluding with the northerners, eyeing our territory. I've got to keep on their movements.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Greetings, esteemed Master of the Jinni.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Regarding the attempt on your life, rest assured, I am still investigating.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I can promise your safety when you are amongst the Tanit, but should you walk the desert sands... Be very careful.

choices.text: About the Eternal Oasis...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Allow me to offer my deepest thanks on behalf of the Tanit and Jeht herself for your deeds...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: The Eternal Oasis not only bears great importance to Jeht, but it also stands as a central pillar of our faith.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Claiming the Eternal Oasis means claiming the sovereignty that once belonged to the Queen of All Oases, Nabu Malikata... For her descendants, this inheritance means everything.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't quite understand... Just what is it actually worth?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Hahaha. Perhaps it can't even be traded for a single coin...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: But it is beyond value nonetheless.

choices.text: Has Jeht been busy?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Yes. As we now hold the Eternal Oasis, we must prevent all with dubious intent from ever breaching its thresholds. The Tanit stands now as defenders of the Eternal Oasis.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: And the one most suited to complete this task is, to my mind, undoubtedly Jeht. She is guarding her parents, is she not?

choices.text: About the traitors...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: I suppose it is due to the fact that we have opened a path to the Eternal Oasis that has caused these traitors to grow restless.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Our goddess, to them, is a symbol of status above all others, and might bring them unfathomable wealth... I cannot tolerate such blasphemy.

choices.text: You still believe she'll wake up.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Of course... Sooner or later, she will reclaim the mantle of her divinity and lead us to become a blooming nation. But before that happens, I... and the Tanit, will continue to serve her will.

choices.text: We went there. She wasn't there.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: She "was" present. You just didn't "see" her. But she "was" and will always "be there."

choices.text: Bye.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Farewell, esteemed Master of the Jinni.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to the marks on the map from Yuften, this must be the right place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's have a look around, maybe the caravan has left some clues!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, what's that over there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Look, over there! It's a rug...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there! It's a cart! We've found the caravan!

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Assassin
dialogues.text: We've also been commissioned to complete a task. You should empathize. Why must you make things so difficult?
